verdict: Symphonic Savagery is the Beethoven of this corpus — technically impeccable, emotionally deranged, and impossible to ignore. The wrestling-to-classical-music mapping is so tight it borders on music theory textbook, but every card earns its place through genuine humor and performative clarity. Named strength: the composer character cards (Wagner's 15-hour match, Cage's 4:33 silence, Tchaikovsky's actual cannon) are some of the best individual cards in the entire Kayfabizarro library. Named weakness: the structural/mechanical cards (Sonata Form, Common Time, Uncommon Time Signatures) lean educational and miss the performative invitation. Table-ready Y.
blurb: For anyone who survived music school, hates elevator Beethoven, or wants to explain the 1913 Rite of Spring riots by staging them at your kitchen table. Klassik Kayfabe at its most savage.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: SYMPHONIC SAVAGERY – The Western Canon as a Cage Match (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Fifty-six cut-and-play cards that drag a thousand years of composers into the same ring and let the room decide who actually earned the standing ovation.

Paris, May 1913. The orchestra starts Le Sacre du Printemps and the audience loses its mind: jeers, fistfights in the aisles, two camps trying to drown each other out while Stravinsky bolts backstage and Nijinsky screams the count from the wings. A century later the same piece is a polite warhorse with a programme note and a cough-sweet intermission. That is what the canon does to everything. It does not preserve the best music, it preserves the fights that got won and then went quiet, sands the danger off, and hands you the corpse in a nice frame. This deck hands the fights back to the table.

Here every name on the syllabus is a fighter on a card. You pick one up, perform their myth out loud with a straight face, and the room rules whether the genius holds or gets hissed off the podium. That is the whole game: Social Story Wrestling for everyone who survived music school, hates elevator Beethoven, and suspects half the canon is reputation wearing a powdered wig.

WHAT'S INSIDE?
- The Symphonic Savagery Core Deck: 56 High-Res "Print, Cut & Play" Cards running the whole bloodline of Western music, featuring Richard Wagner, Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, and John Cage / Minimalism.
- The Freestyle Rules: The complete Anti-Rulebook. No music theory exam, no perfect pitch required, just storytelling, dice-driven chaos, and the one law that every card can claim anything as long as you can sell it before the room calls the bluff.
- The Eras Engine: the deck runs in chronological order, Medieval and Renaissance into Baroque, Classical, Romantic, then the 20th Century and Modernism, so you can wrestle a single rivalry or march the whole argument from plainchant to prepared piano and watch each generation try to murder the one before it.

WHY "PAY WHAT YOU WANT"?
I grew up being handed the canon as a museum: stand back, stay quiet, do not touch the genius. I would rather hand it back as a brawl you are allowed to join. Are you broke, or a student who already spent the rent on reeds and rosin? Enter "0" and take it. Play it. Argue with it out loud. Want to support the craft?
